title: Minimum Jumps to Reach End via Prime Teleportation
summary: Given an integer array nums, starting at index 0, your goal is to reach the last index.
statement: Given an integer array nums, starting at index 0, your goal is to reach the last index. You can perform the following operations: - Adjacent Step: Jump to the next index (i + 1) or the previous index (i - 1), provided the index is within the bounds of the array. - Prime Teleportation: If the value at the current index is a prime number p, you can instantly jump to any other index j where nums[j] is divisible by p. Determine the minimum number of jumps required to reach the last index.
constraints: One to 100,000 values between one and one million.
Adjacent indices are always reachable in one jump.
From a prime value p, teleport to any other index whose value is divisible by p.
target_time_complexity: O(max(nums) log log max + total factors + n)
hints: Array indices form a graph with adjacent edges plus one shared teleport bucket for each prime value present.
Factor values to build divisibility buckets, then run BFS and consume each prime bucket once.
Visit adjacent indices; when the current value is prime, enqueue its bucket and delete that bucket.
BFS gives minimum jumps, and clearing is safe because the first visit already uses that bucket at the smallest possible distance.
editorial: BFS gives minimum jumps, and clearing is safe because the first visit already uses that bucket at the smallest possible distance.

tests.explanation: Step to prime two, then teleport to the final multiple of two.
Step to prime three, then teleport to value nine.
